subject: Coupa invite bounced — SMTP gateway marked message as quarantine
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Coupa invite to Acme bounced (quarantine)

Monica,

Quick heads-up — I attempted to send the Coupa supplier invite to procurement@acme.com at 08:55 PDT but it bounced back with a quarantine designation from their gateway. I attached the bounce_report.txt from our SES webhook.

What I see in the SES feedback: delivery attempted -> quarantined by recipient MTA: "message flagged: probable malware (policy)". No payload attached on our side; invite is a standard coupa-generated link in the body.

Can you check if our invite sender header or DKIM/SPF is being rewritten by our relay? Also including Karthik in case there's a mapping issue for Acme's Coupa tenant (they use a custom SSO config).

Thanks,
Ben

Attachments: bounce_report.txt, coupa_invite.eml

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Coupa invite to Acme bounced (quarantine)

Thanks Ben — looping in Acme procurement and their IT security so we can triage on both sides. Acme, sorry for the noise — we sent a standard Coupa activation invite (link + instructions) from invites@redwood.com. The SES bounce indicates their gateway quarantined it rather than rejecting: likely a content or header heuristic on their side.

Immediate asks:
- Procurement/IT: can you check quarantine logs and allowlist invites@redwood.com and the sending domain redwood-inference.com? If quarantine UI provides a reason string that would help (e.g., "suspicious URL pattern" or "attachment risk").
- Ben/Karthik/Rafael: please share the exact raw MIME we sent (I attached coupa_invite.eml from the SES archive) and confirm DKIM/SPF for invites@redwood.com.

Workaround we can try today: send the invite link wrapped in a plain-text email from an alternate sender (monica.p@redwood.com) and include a short note instructing their admin to click the link. If quarantine blocks links but not plain text, that may get the tenant claiming step started.

I'll stand by for Acme's log snippet. Rafael — can you sanity-check the invite link for any encoded tracking params that could trip heuristics?

— Monica
Director, Customer Onboarding
Redwood Inference

From: Acme IT Security <security@acme.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, acme-gateway-admin@acme.com
Date: 2026-10-29T18:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Coupa invite to Acme bounced (quarantine)

Hi Monica/Ben — thanks for flagging. Our gateway (ProofGate) shows the message was quarantined with the reason code PG-QR-47: "suspicious URL redirect chain". The quarantine UI preserved the original headers; we can see the sender as invites@redwood.com but our gateway rewrote the Return-Path for verification and appended an ARC seal.

A couple of items on our side:
- We can allowlist invites@redwood.com if you prefer; however, we typically prefer allowlisting per-sender+template to limit scope.
- Can you resend the invite with the raw Coupa link (no third-party tracking or shorteners) and a short plain-text-only body? Our heuristics are sensitive to links that look like redirectors.

For speed: we've released the invite out of quarantine and can deliver if you request re-delivery. To avoid recurring quarantines, please:
1) remove any click-tracking parameters from the link;
2) send as plain text;
3) ensure the message From: matches the DKIM-signed domain (prefer invites@redwood.com with d=redwood-inference.com).

If you want us to allowlist, send a signed request from your security contact.

Regards,
Maya Rana
IT Security — Acme Industrial

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Acme IT Security <security@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Coupa invite to Acme bounced (quarantine)

Thanks Maya — appreciate the detail. Quick update from our side after checking coupa_invite.eml:
- The Coupa link is the standard tenant activation URL: https://acme.coupa.com/account_activation?token=LONG_TOKEN&src=redwood-tracking
- We do append a small tracking param (src=redwood-tracking) that helps us correlate open/deliverability for the onboarding flow. We'll remove that param for the resend.
- DKIM/SPF look clean for invites@redwood.com; SES shows pass for both and the attached eml includes the DKIM-Signature header. The ARC seal noted by Acme's gateway is expected when their gateway rewraps for scanning.

Plan:
1) I'll prepare a plain-text resend from invites-no-track@redwood-inference.com with the raw activation URL and subject line "Action required: Complete your supplier activation at Coupa".
2) Monica/Ben — please confirm if invites-no-track@ is acceptable (we'll route replies back into the onboarding queue).
3) Acme IT — once you confirm, we'll request a short allowlist for invites-no-track@ and/or for the redwood-inference.com sending domain.

Rafael
Onboarding Engineer, Redwood Inference
